title: All Ye Nations, Praise the Lord
description: All Ye Nations, Praise the Lord in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 499, “Praise the Lord!”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HEINLEIN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: All ye na-tions, praise the Lord; All ye lands, your voi-ces raise; Heaven and earth, with loud ac-cord, Praise the Lord, for-ev-er praise.

lines: All ye nations, praise the Lord;
All ye lands, your voices raise;
Heaven and earth, with loud accord,
For His truth and mercy stand,
Past, and present, and to be,
Like the years of His right hand,
Praise Him, ye who know His love;
Praise Him, from the depths beneath;
Praise Him in the heights above;
Praise your Maker, all that breathe!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to HEINLEIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
